mainTopic: Is the משנה in מסכת מדות following רבי יהודה? Testing it against רבי יהודה's view that the מזבח stood in the middle of the עזרה.
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי יהודה's ברייתא. The 32-אמה-wide מזבח was lined up exactly with the היכל and its walls: 10 אמות faced the opening and 11 stuck out on each side. רבי יהודה also holds that the מזבח stood in the middle of the עזרה. The גמרא asks whether מסכת מדות can follow רבי יהודה. It quotes the full measurements of the עזרה from מדות, first the length from east to west (187 אמות), then the width from south to north (135 אמות). On the north side of the מזבח was a large slaughtering area, with the rings, tables and pillars. The ramp, and the leftover space, lay to the south. The גמרא ends with a sharp קשיא: by these numbers, most of the מזבח stands in the south, not in the middle. So מדות does not seem to match רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The altar lined up exactly with the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of רבי יהודה's ברייתא. Of the מזבח's 32 אמות, 10 faced the opening of the היכל and 11 stuck out on each side, so the מזבח lined up exactly with the היכל and its walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten cubits were opposite the entrance of the Sanctuary, eleven cubits to the north, and eleven cubits to the south. So the altar was lined up exactly opposite the Sanctuary and its walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יהודה's ברייתא, which describes where the מזבח stood. This is the base text that the next steps will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח was 32 אמות wide (10 + 11 + 11). The opening of the היכל was 10 אמות wide, and the היכל walls plus side areas took up the rest, so the מזבח covered the whole front of the היכל. Since רבי יהודה also says the מזבח stood in the middle of the עזרה, this ברייתא sets up the question of whether מדות agrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, the standard unit of measurement
The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
The outer altar in the courtyard
Lined up exactly, aligned
Its walls

phrases.aramaic: עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: Ten cubits were opposite the entrance of the Sanctuary,
eleven cubits to the north,
and eleven cubits to the south.
It turns out that the altar was lined up
phrases.notes: נִמְצָא literally means 'it comes out'. This is where all the numbers land.

phrases.english: exactly opposite the Sanctuary and its walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא מִזְבֵּחַ מְכֻוּוֹן כְּנֶגֶד הֵיכָל וּכְתָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי יהודה quoted on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the 32-אמה מזבח lined up exactly with the היכל and its walls, and it stood in the middle of the עזרה.

steps.title: Does the altar stand in the middle of the courtyard in מדות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that מסכת מדות follows רבי יהודה, because in מדות the מזבח does not seem to be in the middle of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that מדות follows רבי יהודה, do you find the altar in the middle of the courtyard there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge: מדות does not seem to place the מזבח in the middle of the עזרה. It is setting up the next move, which is to bring the actual measurements from מדות to prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the מזבח was in the middle of the עזרה. If מדות followed him, its measurements should put the מזבח in the middle. The question 'do you find it?' really means 'you don't find it,' so it is an attack, not an innocent question.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you think that...)
מסכת מדות, which records the measurements of the בית המקדש
The Temple courtyard
Do you find it? (meaning: you don't)

steps.confusionAlert: Although this is worded as a question, it is a קשיא. The גמרא is not asking for information. It is claiming that מדות contradicts רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind (to say)
that Middos follows Rabbi Yehuda,
the altar in the middle of the courtyard,
do you find it?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: you do not find it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מִדּוֹת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's claim (the מזבח is in the middle of the עזרה) to test whether מדות follows him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מסכת מדות follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה puts the מזבח in the middle of the עזרה. מדות does not, so מדות cannot be following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: מדות measurements of the courtyard from east to west
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes מדות: the עזרה was 187 by 135 אמות. It then lists the east-to-west breakdown: ישראל 11, כהנים 11, מזבח 32, gap to the אולם 22, היכל 100, and 11 behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: the whole courtyard was 187 cubits long by 135 cubits wide. From east to west it was 187: the area where Israelites walked was 11 cubits; the area where the priests walked was 11 cubits; the altar was 32; between the Entrance Hall and the altar was 22; the Sanctuary was 100 cubits; and there were 11 cubits behind the Holy of Holies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual numbers from מדות to back up its challenge. It starts with the east-to-west length.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This east-to-west list is quoted because it is part of the same משנה, but the challenge does not rest on it. רבי יהודה's 'middle of the עזרה' means midway between north and south, and in every view the מזבח stands east of the היכל. The numbers that decide the question come in the south-to-north list in the next step (step 5 states the conclusion: 'most of the altar stands in the south').

keyTerms.meaning: The place where feet tread (a walking area)
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל
The Holy of Holies, where the ארון and its cover were

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: the entire courtyard was
187 cubits long
by 135 cubits wide.

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַמִּזְרָח לַמַּעֲרָב — מֵאָה וּשְׁמוֹנִים וָשֶׁבַע;
phrases.english: From east to west: 187.

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם דְּרִיסַת רַגְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל — אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה;
phrases.english: The walking area for Israelites: 11 cubits.

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם דְּרִיסַת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה;
phrases.english: The walking area for the priests: 11 cubits.
The altar: 32.
Between the Entrance Hall and the altar: 22.
The Sanctuary: 100 cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת.
phrases.english: And 11 cubits behind the Holy of Holies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: כׇּל הָעֲזָרָה הָיְתָה אוֹרֶךְ מֵאָה וּשְׁמוֹנִים וָשֶׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text that supports the challenge in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The full layout of the עזרה in מדות, beginning with the east-to-west length, which leads into the decisive south-to-north measurements
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת מדות listing the east-to-west measurements of the עזרה

steps.title: מדות measurements of the courtyard from south to north
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with the south-to-north width of 135 אמות. It lists the ramp and מזבח (62), then the gaps and areas on the north side: the rings, tables and pillars. The leftover space lies between the ramp and the southern wall, together with the area of the pillars.
steps.simpleTranslation: From south to north it was 135: the ramp and the altar together were 62; from the altar to the rings, 8 cubits; the area of the rings, 24; from the rings to the tables, 4; from the tables to the pillars, 4; from the pillars to the courtyard wall, 8 cubits. The rest was between the ramp and the wall, plus the area of the pillars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting מדות, now giving the width from south to north. This sets up the final punch of the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: North of the מזבח was the slaughtering area (rings, tables and pillars), which took up a lot of room. The ramp ran south from the מזבח. Laid out this way, the מזבח ends up shifted toward the southern half of the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח (on its south side)
Rings in the floor used to hold animals for שחיטה
Tables where the meat and innards were rinsed
Short pillars where animals were hung for skinning
The remainder, the leftover space

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַדָּרוֹם לַצָּפוֹן — מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ;
phrases.english: From south to north: 135.
The ramp and the altar: 62.
From the altar to the rings: 8 cubits.
The area of the rings: 24.
From the rings to the tables: 4.
From the tables to the pillars: 4.

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַנַּנָּסִין לְכוֹתֶל עֲזָרָה — שְׁמוֹנֶה אַמּוֹת;
phrases.english: From the pillars to the courtyard wall: 8 cubits.
And the remainder was between the ramp and the (southern) wall,
phrases.notes: Adding it up: 62 + 8 + 24 + 4 + 4 + 8 = 110, which leaves 25 of the 135.

phrases.english: and the area taken up by the pillars themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הַדָּרוֹם לַצָּפוֹן — מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה from מדות, moving from the length to the width.
steps.raayaObject: The position of the מזבח along the south-north axis
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת מדות listing the south-to-north measurements

steps.title: Most of the altar stands in the south
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its challenge and sharpens it. By the measurements in מדות, most of the מזבח stands in the southern part of the עזרה, so it is not in the middle as רבי יהודה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that מדות follows רבי יהודה, do you find the altar in the middle of the courtyard? Most of the altar stands in the south!
steps.whatsHappening: Having laid out the numbers, the גמרא repeats its challenge with the punchline: most of the מזבח is in the south. Therefore מדות does not fit רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the words of step 2, but now with proof attached. Step 2 only claimed the מזבח was not in the middle. This step points to the exact problem: the south-north layout pushes most of the מזבח into the southern half, which contradicts רבי יהודה's 'middle of the עזרה.'

keyTerms.meaning: The majority, most of something
Stands, is located
South

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the מזבח stood in the middle of the עזרה. The measurements in מסכת מדות put most of the מזבח in the south. So the גמרא challenges the idea that מדות follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Identifying whose opinion an anonymous משנה follows (here, מסכת מדות) decides which other rulings and descriptions of the מקדש fit with it.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind (to say)
that Middos follows Rabbi Yehuda,
the altar in the middle of the courtyard,
do you find it?
Why, most of the altar stands in the south!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the challenge from the measurements just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מסכת מדות follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה says the מזבח is in the middle of the עזרה. The measurements in מדות place most of the מזבח in the south, so the two cannot match.
